title: Field kickoff - tunnel & infra quirks journal
body:
Quick context:
- Customer: NovaHealth (prod workload will be in eu-west-1 equivalent private region)
- Deployment: private (VPC), single colocation cage + cloud peering, inline HSM for keys, onprem Docker+K8s 1.25.
- Contact: NetEng: Priya K., Security: Dan S. (on call M-F 09-17 local)

Top goals for kickoff day (keeps me focused):
- Get base cluster into customer network with minimal blast radius
- Confirm tunnel and bastion working for admin ops and image pulls
- Verify KMS/HSM signing handshake with customer HSM appliance
- Smoke-run redwood runtime (simple echo model) behind their ALB

Immediate checklist (order matters):
1) Preflight - on my laptop before onsite
  - ssh keys: ensure new key pair (rh-field-2026) exists and pushed to Ops vault
  - docker pull test: try pulling from our ACR via customer's peering path (curl registry auth endpoint)
  - certs: have customer CA bundle; create TLS bundle local copy at /tmp/nova-ca.pem

2) Network handshake (with Priya) - minutes 0-30 after arrival\  - confirm CIDR blocks: their data plane 10.20.0.0/16, ours 172.16.0.0/16; must avoid overlap
  - route tables: ensure route to colo appliance for 172.16.0.0/16 via transit-gw (customer confirmed)
  - MTU: they run jumbo frames; set MTU 9001 on tunnel interfaces; common source of broken grpc connections

3) Bastion and tunnels\  - they prefer wireguard for latency; fallback to IPsec if customer appliance forbids wireguard
  - ephemeral bastion: provision t2.small-equivalent VM in customer subnet, restrict to our CIDR 172.16.0.0/28
  - keep port-forward rule notes: local -> remote kubectl proxy via 127.0.0.1:8001 forwarded to kube-apiserver 6443 over bastion tunnel

Commands I use repeatedly (put in ~/.local/bin/field_kit later):
- check k8s nodes: kubectl --context=field-nova get nodes -o wide
- tail pods in runtime ns: kubectl -n redwood logs -f deploy/runtime --since=10m
- test model endpoint: curl -s -k https://10.20.8.15:8443/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
- verify HSM: openssl s_client -connect hsm.local:9443 -CAfile /tmp/nova-ca.pem

Observed quirks (today / predicted):
- MTU mismatch breaks chunked responses and long streaming. if streaming stalls, check if tcpdump shows MTU drops. quick fix: set GRPC_MAX_RECEIVE_MESSAGE_LENGTH low? not ideal. Prefer lower MTU on workload iface.
- Customer proxy rewrites SNI; image pulls fail with TLS mismatch. Workaround: use their internal mirror (they provided mirror URL) or configure registry to use IP with Host header override via docker config.
- SELinux was Enforcing on node image; initial containerd crashes until we set proper SELinux context on runtime socket. Add note to node bootstrap: setenforce 0 only as last resort — prefer fix with chcon.
- HSM appliance requires client certs signed by their CA; our cert rotation script must push certchain in 2 steps (sign -> verify -> install). Need to coordinate with Dan for CSR acceptance window.

Blockers to escalate (if not resolved in 2 hours):
- image pull cannot complete over peering and customer mirror is rate-limited -> escalate to Priya and request temporary S3 presigned image buckets.
- HSM handshake failing with 'unknown ca' -> need customer's ops to confirm CA bundle applied to the appliance truststore (ticket: PD-842

Field hacks & small scripts
- small helper to test MTU path (run from bastion):
  iperf3 -c 10.20.8.15 -M 9001 -t 5
- quick wireguard check: wg showconf wg0 | grep Peer -A2 to confirm endpoint
- check kernel driver for NVIDIA: nvidia-smi || cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version

Deployment notes (do in stages):
A) minimal runtime (single replica, no cache layer) -> confirm inference basic generate works\B) enable kv-cache and batching slow -> observe tail latency and increase replica count
C) enable quantized model variant and test regression against eval promptset (small set)

Troubleshooting snippets (copy these into ticket replies):
- If 'kubelet auth' fails with 401: verify kube-apiserver certs on node + kubelet client cert and system time (NTP out of sync causes 401s). run chronyd -q if needed.
- If docker pull times out but ping works: check their transparent proxy (squid) logs and confirm CONNECT method allowed for registry domain.

To-do (next actions, prioritized):
- [ ] Push field_kit helpers to repo (ash to review) - target EOD
- [ ] Confirm HSM CSR window with Dan and get their accepted CSR hash - today
- [ ] Add MTU note to public runbook and create automated MTU probe in bootstrap scripts
- [ ] Ship temporary image mirror instructions to Priya in Slack + escalate if throttle persists

Notes to self:
- Keep minimal scope for first smoke. Resist enabling autoscaling until caching is validated.
- Take video of ephemeral load balancer flow (for postmortem).
- If anything looks flaky, capture tcpdump for 30s and upload to shared folder (file prefix nova-field-YYYYMMDD-).

End of day quick log (timestamps approximate):
- 09:12 Arrived, handoff with Priya, verified CIDRs
- 10:05 Bastion up, wireguard handshake succeeded (peer added)
- 11:40 First image pull failed, found transparent proxy rewrite; switched to internal mirror
- 13:05 HSM cert rejected; Dan applied CA bundle at 14:50 and handshake succeeded on 14:52
- 15:20 Run smoke: simple generate returned 200, streaming partial frames had stalls (MTU)
- 16:00 Lowered MTU on workload iface to 1400, streaming stabilized
- 16:30 Packed up, briefed customer, follow-ups created (see linked artifacts)

Quick wins for next visits:
- Request permanent NTP peer from customer to avoid clock drift
- Get a small puppet/ansible snippet to idempotently set MTU and SELinux contexts

Tagged follow-ups: PD-842 (HSM), PD-857 (network mirror), PD-861 (runtime SELinux)

Random scratch thoughts:
- Maybe include a health endpoint that checks MTU and reports suggested iface MTU to ops during bootstrap. low friction.
- Consider distributing a tiny sidecar to detect proxy rewrite on TLS SNI and log mismatch to our observability agent.

-- maya
